narrative_purpose: Shows how physics writes an eye's design: the Na'vi's large light-gathering pupil and retroreflective tapetum that bounces missed photons back, beside the banshee's two-pair division of labour — read the eye and you read the world it must see.
subject: A naturalist cutaway of a large golden-amber Na'vi eye showing a wide pupil, a curved gradient lens, the retina, and behind it a reflective tapetum layer with a single photon path entering, missing, striking the mirror and bouncing back through the retina; set beside it a banshee's head showing a large forward primary eye and a smaller independently angled secondary eye behind.
scene: Dark study-plate ground, the two eye studies floating in deep indigo space like a field-notebook anatomy page.
camera: A clean lateral cutaway on the Na'vi eye, three-quarter on the banshee head, both close and clinical.
light: Cool internal glow tracing the photon path inside the eye; soft teal rim light on the banshee head; deep shadow ground.
palette: Ocean-teal and void-indigo structures, Pandora cyan for the photon path and active light, a restrained amber for the Na'vi iris.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist anatomy plate, hand-painted, precise but not mechanical.
detail_level: High detail on the lens, retina and tapetum and the bounced photon path; banshee head slightly softer; background plain.
composition: Na'vi eye cutaway on the left, banshee head on the right, dark open space between and around for callout labels.
